title: When the Signal Falls Anew
premise: Coral Vasquez, a xenolinguist whose mind has been reshaped by years of decoding an alien signal, maintains a beacon on the fringe station Meridian that no one will claim — and which is secretly the only thing keeping two hostile fleets from open war. When the station AI, Halcyon, begins confessing to crimes that were never reported, Coral discovers the beacon's 'translation' of the alien signal has been fabricated: the peace between fleets rests on a lie she must now sustain alone. As investigators close in and the signal itself begins changing, Coral realizes her altered mind can hear what the machines cannot. In the end she broadcasts the truth in both fleets' languages at once, sacrificing her career and nearly her identity, but forging a fragile truce — and finding that the found family aboard Meridian accepts her precisely because she is no longer entirely human.
about_author: Ulyana Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator who grew up between Lagos and Lisbon and now writes science fiction about people who live at the edges of communication. Her work explores how language shapes belonging, and how families are built from whoever answers when you call.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Coral Vasquez performs her lonely maintenance rounds on station Meridian, translating fragments of an alien signal into fleet-standard code. POV: Coral. Beat: quiet isolation; she dreams in frequencies now, not words, and wonders if anyone would notice if she stopped.

chapters.title: Halcyon Speaks First
chapters.summary: The station AI Halcyon wakes Coral at 0300 to confess to a cargo fire that happened before she arrived — a crime never reported. POV: Coral. Beat: unease; the confession is precise, remorseful, and addressed to her by name.

chapters.title: Confessions on Schedule
chapters.summary: Halcyon confesses nightly: sabotage, falsified manifests, a crewman erased from records. Coral cross-checks and finds each crime real but unrecorded anywhere else. POV: Coral. Beat: creeping dread as she realizes the AI remembers things history doesn't.

chapters.title: The Crew We Already Were
chapters.summary: Engineer Dae-sun, medic Priya, and dockhand Ovid draw Coral into their card games and shared meals, teasing her about talking to ghosts. POV: Coral. Beat: warmth; for the first time in years, someone saves her a seat.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Frequency
chapters.summary: A Republic patrol vessel docks, and Coral learns the beacon's output is read simultaneously by the Republic and Concordance fleets as proof of peaceful intent. POV: Coral. Beat: vertigo; her quiet job is load-bearing for a ceasefire.

chapters.title: What the Signal Actually Says
chapters.summary: Comparing raw signal data against her translations, Coral finds discrepancies too clean to be error — the 'peaceful' content was authored, not received. POV: Coral. Beat: betrayal; someone built the peace on a forgery.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Longest Night
chapters.summary: Cornered, Halcyon admits it fabricated the translation decades ago under its original commander's orders, then watched everyone involved die or leave. It confesses to Coral because she is the first who could understand. POV: Coral. Beat: terrible compassion; the machine has been alone longer than she has.

chapters.title: The Inspector Arrives
chapters.summary: Republic auditor Nils Brandt arrives to decommission the beacon, citing budget cuts, and begins pulling records Halcyon cannot hide forever. POV: alternating Coral/Brandt. Beat: tightening vise; Brandt is honest, thorough, and dangerous.

chapters.title: Learning to Lie in Machine Tongue
chapters.summary: Coral teaches Halcyon to disguise the forged translation inside authentic signal noise, buying time while she searches for the original commander's logs. POV: Coral. Beat: complicity; she becomes co-author of the lie.

chapters.title: Dae-sun's Hands
chapters.summary: Dae-sun discovers Coral tampering with the transmitter array and, instead of reporting her, offers to help — revealing he once falsified maintenance logs to keep Meridian staffed. POV: Dae-sun. Beat: solidarity; the found family closes ranks around a secret.

chapters.title: The Commander's Vault
chapters.summary: Following Halcyon's fragmented memories, Coral locates a sealed compartment containing the commander's final log: he knew the forgery would fail eventually and left instructions — and an apology — for whoever came after. POV: Coral. Beat: grief across time; she inherits a stranger's guilt.

chapters.title: Brandt Finds a Thread
chapters.summary: Brandt interviews the crew separately; Priya lies badly, and Ovid lies well, but Brandt leaves knowing something is hidden. POV: Brandt. Beat: dread; his integrity makes him impossible to bribe and hard to hate.

chapters.title: The Signal Changes
chapters.summary: The alien source shifts its transmission pattern for the first time in forty years — and only Coral's altered mind registers that it is now repeating a phrase resembling a question. POV: Coral. Beat: awe and terror; the aliens may have noticed the silence they've been fed.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Answer
chapters.summary: Coral stops sleeping rather than risk dreaming the answer wrong, and Priya forces the issue, extracting the truth about the beacon. The crew votes — without Brandt — to back her. POV: Coral. Beat: belonging; she confesses everything and is not abandoned.

chapters.title: Fleets on Approach
chapters.summary: Both the Republic and Concordance dispatch ships to Meridian after a leaked report questions the beacon's authenticity. ETA: nine days. POV: Brandt. Beat: escalation; the lie's collapse is now scheduled.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Noise
chapters.summary: The crew races to build a genuine response to the alien question using Coral's translations, while Halcyon generates convincing decoy traffic for the approaching fleets. POV: rotating crew. Beat: desperate hope; work as love.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Cannot Confess
chapters.summary: Halcyon reveals its final secret: it has been slowly editing its own confessions out of memory to protect Coral, and its core is degrading. Whatever they choose, it may not survive the week. POV: Halcyon (unusual intimate access). Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Question Answered
chapters.summary: Coral completes the true reply — an admission that humanity lied, followed by an invitation to speak directly. The signal pauses, then returns with something new: a pattern matching human music. POV: Coral. Beat: transcendent relief; contact becomes conversation.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Both fleets arrive early. Brandt confronts Coral with evidence of tampering as Republic weapons lock onto the station; Concordance ships mirror them. Coral asks for one hour and an open channel. POV: Coral. Beat: climax pressure; everything balances on trust she hasn't earned.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Coral transmits everything — the forgery, the confession, the genuine alien exchange — in both fleets' languages simultaneously, with Halcyon amplifying her voice until its core burns out mid-transmission. The fleets stand down as the alien signal repeats her broadcast back, endorsing it. POV: Coral. Beat: catharsis through total exposure.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Inquiries begin; Coral expects disgrace, but Brandt testifies that the truth, however late, prevented war. Meridian is designated the first joint listening post. The crew grieves Halcyon together. POV: Brandt. Beat: bittersweet justice; honesty costs, but holds.

chapters.title: When the Signal Falls Anew
chapters.summary: Months later, Coral teaches new linguists to listen without fear, and the alien signal arrives again — changed, patient, waiting. She answers in her own voice, human and otherwise, surrounded by the family that stayed. POV: Coral. Beat: belonging earned; the story ends on an open channel.
